newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers neutral on debt market - MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers neutral on debt market - MCM.

text.p: More U.S. fixed-income managers experienced cash outflows, but had a "neutral" outlook on the debt market over the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
In the week ending July 14, cash as a percentage of assets rose to 3.09 percent from 3.07 percent registered the previous week.

In addition, durations as a percentage of benchmark remained steady at 108.1 percent, the same as the previous week. A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 29 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," lower than 31 percent in the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" dropped to 15 percent from 19 percent the previous week.
Fifty-six percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 50 percent the prior week.
The survey showed 32 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, while 10.0 percent underweighted it, with both figures holding steady from the previous week.
The remaining 58 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 49 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 10 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
